messages:
jordan: hey team :wave: first day, trying to access the dev k8s cluster but `kubectl get pods -n team-foo` gives 'Forbidden'. I think my kubeconfig is set but not sure which context I'm on.

maria: welcome jordan! :tada: quick checks — which context do you have? `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts` please.

jordan: current-context shows `redwood-dev/user-jordan`, `kubectl get-contexts` lists 3 contexts: redwood-prod, redwood-staging, redwood-dev/user-jordan (star on that one)

maria: OK that means your local kubeconfig has a dev context. Forbidden usually means RBAC. Can you run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-foo` and paste output?

jordan: ran it: "no" — so yeah looks like I don't have list perms.

ben: hey @maria — tagging infra oncall. Jordan, did you file the new-hires infra access form? We auto-add folks to the `eng-new-hires` group which has view access in `team-foo` namespace.

jordan: i filled the general onboarding form yesterday, but didn't see a specific infra form link. Is that different?

maria: yep there is a short infra access form — link is internal: https://redwood.corp/onboard/infra-access. It asks for GitHub handle, manager, and namespaces. Fill that and choose "k8s-dev". Once submitted the RBAC job runs and you should get a ClusterRoleBinding within ~15 min.

jordan: submitted now. while I wait, is there a way to test without exposing prod creds? also noticed my kubeconfig has SSO provider blocks — `exec` auth.

ben: SSO exec is normal. If you need to share a kubeconfig for debugging, do NOT copy the whole file. Use `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > /tmp/jordan-kube.yaml` to produce a flattened config that contains only the current context and no local file refs. Then you can redact the token if you must share.

maria: also for quick checks you can run `kubectl auth can-i --list -n team-foo` after the form completes. If still blocked ping me or @ben and include output of `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.contexts[0].name}'` and the `can-i` result.

sre-bot: infra-access-job started for user=jordan namespace=team-foo (job id: ia-20274). You will receive an update in ~10-15m.

jordan: saw the bot, nice. thanks. one more question: my dev context keeps switching when I use a couple of projects. How do I pin a context per repo?

maria: use a `.kubeconfig` in the repo and set `KUBECONFIG=./.kubeconfig` in dir, or create a dir-specific wrapper: `direnv` + `export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/.kubeconfig:$HOME/.kube/config`. We recommend the flattened per-project file approach so you don't accidentally hit prod contexts.

ben: infra job completed — you should have `view` role in `team-foo`. Jordan run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n team-foo` now.

jordan: works! `yes` now. :relieved: thanks for the quick help. one last ask — any simple docs for common k8s onboarding steps I should bookmark?

maria: quick cheat sheet: https://redwood.corp/devx/k8s-onboard (contains commands we mentioned, how to request access, and who to ping). If anything else blocks you ping #eng-oncall or @maria directly.

jordan: saved. appreciate it :100:
